newsitem.title: UK: Suspects in French bombing lose extradition appeal.
newsitem.headline: Suspects in French bombing lose extradition appeal.

text.p: Two men accused of helping plot a wave of bombings that terrorised France in 1995 lost their appeal on Wednesday against extradition to France.

Algerian Rachid Ramda and Mustapha Boutarfa, who has dual French and Algerian nationality, had appealed to Britain's High Court against extradition, claiming they would not get a fair trial in "anti-Moslem" France.
The two judges at Wednesday's hearing ruled there was no evidence that the French courts would be biased.
"I do not find a risk of any lack of fairness at the trial or trials of either of the applicants," Judge Sir Malcolm Pill told the court.
Ramda, 27, was described in the French press as the man responsible for organising the financing of the bombings in Paris, Lyon and Lille between July and November 1995.
In the most serious attack, seven people were killed by a bomb on the Paris Metro.
Ramda has been held for the past year in Belmarsh, the top security prison outside London designed to hold IRA prisoners.
Boutarfa is reported to have fled Paris following the arrest of another man implicated in the bombings.
Lawyers said they expected the men to take their appeal to Britain's highest court, the House of Lords.
